bug_semantics: An authenticated low-privilege viewer (or any request admitted by the outer authentication proxy) could send DELETE /api/users/{username}. The route performed no role/ownership authorization and unconditionally deleted the selected User row, so a viewer could delete other accounts, including the built-in admin, causing integrity loss and administrative denial of service.
flaw_origin: PR #11347 member fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497 first added the persistent User model and the DELETE /users/<username> handler in frigate/api/auth.py:248-251 as a bare route calling User.delete_by_id(username).execute(), without an admin-role dependency or protection for the admin account. Its direct parent had no user-management routes at all. The PR was later squash-landed as 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def; the later viewer-role work in 74ca009b0b767a8393562a932673f8fd5b11b7fe made the latent missing per-action authorization exploitable by a formally low-privilege role but did not originate the delete handler.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object identifies author Blake Blackshear (@blakeblackshear) and committer Blake Blackshear (@blakeblackshear), has the message "move users to database instead of config", an empty body, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/security/advisories/GHSA-vg28-83rp-8xx4 identifies CWE-285, DELETE /api/users/admin, affected 0.16.2, patched 0.16.3, and recommends dependencies=[Depends(require_role(["admin"]))]. The release page https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/releases/tag/v0.16.3 says exploitation requires authenticated access and that this advisory was addressed in 0.16.3.

Squash decomposition: refs/pull/11347/head resolved to 20b9a85b89a834df886240e4e6f738824454333d. GitHub blame on that preserved PR head, https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/blame/20b9a85b89a834df886240e4e6f738824454333d/frigate/api/auth.py, traces the user-management block to member fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497. The member diff at https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/commit/fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497 adds frigate/api/auth.py lines 248-251: @AuthBp.route("/users/<username>", methods=["DELETE"]), def delete_user(username: str), User.delete_by_id(username).execute(), and a success response, with no authorization guard.

Direct-parent verification: the BIC commit object names parent 7cf3abc850ca3cd335203a5654d801e58a2cc816. The complete parent version of frigate/api/auth.py at https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/blob/7cf3abc850ca3cd335203a5654d801e58a2cc816/frigate/api/auth.py ends after login and contains no /users route, delete_user function, or User.delete_by_id call. Thus the vulnerable handler is absent from the immediate parent tree.

Main-history confirmation: git log -L 449,453:frigate/api/auth.py v0.16.2 traced the persisted delete function through FastAPI conversion cffc431bf0a874d512ab0c01731a618cbcd1f099 back to squash landing 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def; that landing's parent a70dd02788685ca7e345ce921df08429d27807e3 has no frigate/api/auth.py (git ls-tree returned no entry). git tag --contains 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def includes v0.14.0 through v0.16.2, so the flawed handler predates the affected boundary rather than being a release-only change.

Privilege activation: https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/commit/74ca009b0b767a8393562a932673f8fd5b11b7fe introduced viewer-role claims and require_role, protected GET/POST user administration, but left DELETE /users/{username} unchanged. git tag --contains 74ca009b0b767a8393562a932673f8fd5b11b7fe includes v0.16.0, v0.16.1, and v0.16.2. At v0.16.2, git blame of frigate/api/auth.py:450-453 shows an unguarded route and unconditional User.delete_by_id.

Direct fix: https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/commit/592c245dcd25919e7d39bdae2462847c6323850f changes frigate/api/auth.py to require Depends(require_role(["admin"])) on DELETE /users/{username} and rejects username == "admin" with HTTP 403. Its direct parent 914ff4f1e5c2a15e93c8b61d317c9e5ffa141ae3 still has the unguarded route. git rev-list --ancestry-path v0.16.2..v0.16.3 -- frigate/api/auth.py returns this commit as the sole auth.py change; git tag --contains it begins at v0.16.3. Tag objects resolve to v0.16.2=4d582062fba09f69fb40658fbe02b4f527dc46af and v0.16.3=90344540b30529d7d2d38e304577418281965b5a.

Fixed-tree verification: git blame v0.16.3 -- frigate/api/auth.py:450-457 attributes the admin dependency and built-in-admin refusal to 592c245dcd25919e7d39bdae2462847c6323850f, while the destructive line remains below them and is unreachable to viewers or for username admin.

BIC-only AI attribution source: the embedded commit object at https://github.com/blakeblackshear/frigate/commit/fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497 reports author and committer Blake Blackshear, parent 7cf3abc850ca3cd335203a5654d801e58a2cc816, message "move users to database instead of config", and an empty body; it contains no AI authorship/co-authorship/generation marker.
reasoning: The advisory's destructive action is the user-delete handler, not the later framework conversion or release commit. Decomposing PR #11347 is necessary because the main-history commit 1133202cbd12ec6a92fa1b446889ff2d75986def is a squash aggregate. The preserved PR-head blame and member diff identify fafc0aab2fea3ec3eab86fb3a2b02629ca0de497 as the smallest member that first wrote both the arbitrary-username DELETE route and the database deletion operation. Its direct parent contains neither user-management endpoints nor the destructive call, satisfying direct-parent absence. The handler survived the FastAPI rewrite; 74ca009b0b767a8393562a932673f8fd5b11b7fe later established viewer/admin separation but omitted DELETE from the protected user routes, making the latent flaw reachable by viewers. In v0.16.2 the route remained unguarded. Commit 592c245dcd25919e7d39bdae2462847c6323850f directly closes both facets—admin-only authorization and non-deletability of the built-in admin—and is the only auth.py change on the v0.16.2-to-v0.16.3 ancestry path. Because the exact decomposed BIC commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker, the BIC-only attribution verdict is NOT_AI.
